title: Parkland Formula for Burns
sources: Baxter CR, Shires T. Ann N Y Acad Sci 1968
purpose: First-24-hour crystalloid volume for burn resuscitation. Give half in the first 8 hours from the time of the burn, the rest over the next 16 hours. Titrate to urine output.

inputs.label: % total body surface area burned (2nd degree and deeper)

interpretation.label: This is a starting estimate only — titrate to a urine output of 0.5 mL/kg/h (adults) or 1 mL/kg/h (children < 30 kg).

notes: Clock starts at the time of the burn, not arrival — subtract elapsed time when setting the first-8-hour rate. Modified Brooke (2 mL/kg/%TBSA) is an alternative lower-volume strategy some centres prefer.
